name: Parula Blue
lede: Parula Blue is a muted slate blue named for the parula warblers, small American songbirds whose backs carry close to this exact grey-blue.

sections.title: A warbler's back
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 color standards, written by an ornithologist who also founded the field's standard color reference, record this swatch on plate XLII, hue 45 [1]. Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary independently records the same name, first dated to 1912, on plate 36 [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS system, citing both, classes it in block 186 [1]. The parulas themselves, a family that includes the Northern Parula and a scatter of closely related American warblers, carry this grey-blue mainly across the back and wings, with brighter yellow underneath, so the name borrows only the muted half of the bird [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[ether]], [[celestial-blue]], [[grey-blue]] and [[deep-orient-blue]], at 5.5, 5.5, [[denim]] and [[grey]] sit nearby in the same muted-blue family [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match to Parula Blue in 235 of 23,781 paintings (0.99 percent), as photographed, split fairly evenly between highlight and midtone roles [2]. It is strongly over-represented in work by Adriaen van de Velde, Gustave Caillebotte and Vincent van Gogh, each well over ten times the archive average [2]. It keeps company with Slate and Denim more than chance [2]. These are screen approximations of aged, varnished canvases, not pigment identifications [2].

origin.first_recorded: Ridgway, 1912, plate XLII; also Maerz and Paul, 1930, first recorded 1912
